viewer-refresh: A viewer asked for its display's refresh only at connect, so a Smooth session whose window moved from a 120 Hz to a 60 Hz screen kept encoding and sending 120 fps, and Windows viewers on 59.94 or 119.88 Hz modes asked for whole rates. Every desktop viewer now follows the refresh of the display its window is on, exactly, and tells the host through the FpsCap message every peer already accepts.
decoder-install-hints: A Windows viewer whose GPU decodes HEVC but lacks Microsoft's HEVC Video Extensions ran every session on H.264, and a Linux viewer without GStreamer's decoders fell back to JPEG at 8 FPS. The viewer now names the install that would give it the better codec (the HEVC extension, GStreamer's decoders or a GPU video driver) while a session goes without it, and a hint dismissed on the device stays dismissed.
viewer-scroll: Each embedder reports a wheel notch as a different distance, so one notch scrolled a different amount on every viewer, and fine trackpad scrolling was rounded to whole notches. A wheel notch is now one host notch on every viewer; a host that lists wheel_hires (Windows and macOS) receives scrolls in 1/120 of a notch with trackpad momentum, older hosts keep whole notches, and the Windows helper carries the scroll in helper protocol 12 (.v12 pipes), so the desktop service needs Update.
mac-vt-padded-capture: VideoToolbox encodes a picture whose size is not a multiple of 16 through an internal copy, which made the dwell longer at common Retina sizes. A Mac host now captures such sizes into a 16-padded surface and crops the padding in the SPS, which every viewer's decoder honours, so VideoToolbox takes its aligned path at every size.
encoder-throughput-cap: When an encoder slower than the pace still accepts input, four units queue and each waits behind three: an 11 ms encoder at pace 120 dwells about 44 ms, unevenly. The host now caps its pace at the encoder's measured throughput while units queue four deep, so dwell falls back to one or two service times with even spacing, and lifts the cap when the encoder keeps up.
host-direct-bbr: BBR could keep a direct video path's throughput under random loss where Cubic backs off. The host's direct QUIC connections were measured with BBR and Cubic under loss, delay and a policer, open loop and with receipt-driven rate control: BBR helped under random loss but lost many times more packets behind a policer, so Cubic stays. The harness and the record remain for a later attempt.
linux-video-plane: Every Linux viewer presented at most 60 frames a second through Flutter's fixed timer, each picture waiting for it unsynchronised with the display. A GTK GL video plane under a transparent Flutter view draws the newest picture whenever GTK draws the window, at the display's refresh where the compositor paces it. It is opt-in (--dart-define=presenter=plane) until a Linux device measures it.
mac-viewer-enhance: A 1080p or 1440p host shown full screen on a Retina or 4K display is enlarged bilinearly, so its text is soft. The Mac viewer's Core Animation presenter can now upscale an enlarged picture on the GPU with clamped Catmull-Rom and sharpen its luma (off, low, medium, high), set by a shared 'Sharpen enlarged picture' preference that is off by default.
linux-plane-scaling: Shrinking a large remote into a small window aliased its text, and enlarging it was soft. The Linux video plane now scales down by area averaging, and when enlarging applies the shared 'Sharpen enlarged picture' level with the same Catmull-Rom and luma sharpening as the Mac. The Flutter texture fallback keeps bilinear.
